title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident shows a deliberate attempt to poison the inputs that AI systems draw on when generating responses. The operation worked by manufacturing a high volume of documents designed to look like credible academic output, then using a service built specifically to make that content visible to AI retrieval and training pipelines. The failure this exposes is not inside the AI models themselves but upstream of them, at the point where systems ingest or cite web content without verifying the institutional identity of the source. An AI chatbot citing a document from a nonexistent think tank is behaving as designed, because the design assumes sources are what they claim to be.

The scale of the content, more than 560,000 words produced in nine days, suggests the operation was calibrated to the volume thresholds that affect how prominently content appears in both search results and AI outputs. Catching this kind of manipulation would require source verification at the infrastructure level, checking whether a named institution legally exists before its publications are weighted as authoritative. That check was not present, and the content reached AI systems and search indexes regardless.

What is not established is whether the operation successfully altered the outputs of any specific AI system in a measurable way, or changed public opinion, and the reporting itself notes Israeli officials considered it ineffective.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
A fake American think tank funded by Israel published over 560,000 words in nine days to influence artificial intelligence chatbots into promoting pro-Israel arguments. The Hanover Institute for Public Policy, which does not legally exist, created 124 reports framed as academic research addressing contentious topics like alleged Israeli war crimes and genocide in Gaza. The reports were strategically designed to appear in chatbot training data and search results, using a platform called Res that specializes in "generative engine optimization" to ensure AI systems cite the content.

The operation represents part of a broader Israeli government campaign costing tens of millions of dollars, routed through advertising company Havas Media and contractors including Trump's former campaign manager Brad Parscale. The Hanover Institute was registered with the US Justice Department as foreign agent propaganda material in August 2026. Israeli officials have expressed frustration about the campaign's ineffectiveness, with public opinion polling showing Americans increasingly sympathize with Palestinians rather than Israel. Researchers warn the effort demonstrates a new threat of foreign governments manipulating AI systems to shape online narratives without detection or fact-checking capability.
